title: Which year was it, going back past year one?
description: Three year questions are solved by moving left or right on a line of years, taking away to go back and counting that there is no year zero. The video breaks the slip of reading a plain negative number as the BCE year without allowing for the missing year zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: going back in time means subtracting, and the year line skips zero, so a result below zero needs one more for its BCE year. Watch for students who write minus one hundred seventy four as one hundred seventy four BCE.

video_script.why: The child subtracts years to go back in time and allows for the missing year zero when the answer falls before year one.
video_script.substitution: The book's three year questions on a line of years, with the present year taken as 2026 as the worklist does.
video_script.anchor: a line of years with year one in the middle and BCE years on its left
video_script.payoff_line: The three years are eighteen seventy six, one hundred seventy five BCE and three hundred sixty BCE

final_answer.value: a. 1876; b. 175 BCE; c. 360 BCE (present year 2026)
final_answer.spoken: eighteen seventy six, one hundred seventy five BCE and three hundred sixty BCE

hold_back: a. 1876; b. 175 BCE; c. 360 BCE (present year 2026)
never_show: the year for each part before its step
maths_rules: b: 2026 − 2200 = −174 on a plain number line
b: there is no year 0, so the BCE year is one more than the plain number: 175 BCE
b check: from 175 BCE, 175 steps reach year 1 and 2025 more steps reach 2026; 175 + 2025 = 2200
c: 680 − 320 = 360, so 360 BCE (moving right, the BCE number falls)
video_script.design: One line of years. Year one sits in the middle with BCE years to its left and no zero place. Each part of the question is a jump along the line.
open_questions: The book does not name the present year in the question; the worklist takes it as 2026 and this script follows that.
